oldPassage.text:
- **Runs when:** mọi lần `git commit` chạm cây chính — dù người gõ tay, một trợ lý,
  hay CI — đi qua một hook cài sẵn ở tầng git (không phải một verb fgOS, không phải
  một cấu hình riêng của công cụ trợ lý nào).
- **Blocked when:** đèn hoạt động (beacon, `.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json`)
  ghi rằng một danh tính KHÁC đã commit ở cây chính này trong cửa sổ `windowMs` chính
  người ghi khai (mặc định 20 s, đè được qua `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) — commit
  bị từ chối thẳng; hoặc một writer fgOS (claim, checkpoint, land) đang giữ khóa kernel
  `main-checkout` (`<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock`) mà commit này không phải con mượn
  — hook thử khóa MỘT lần bằng description riêng, không bao giờ chờ, rồi từ chối. Đèn
  hỏng thì ngược lại: chỉ là gợi ý, nên cảnh báo rồi cho qua. Commit của chính fgOS
  (git con chạy qua `runBorrowed`: `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` chỉ đúng slot, slot cùng
  `dev:ino` với file khóa, `flock` không chờ trên slot thành công) bỏ qua đèn, không ghi đèn.
- **What changes:** khi cây chính đang rảnh, hoặc khi CHÍNH danh tính đang commit là
  danh tính đã ghi khóa gần nhất (cùng phiên tiếp tục làm việc), commit đi qua bình
  thường, không thông báo gì. Danh tính ưu tiên biến môi trường phiên trợ lý khi có;
  vắng mặt (terminal tay gõ) thì suy ra từ một tiến trình tổ tiên gần đó — suy đoán
  tốt-nhất, không tuyệt đối (hai terminal tay gõ chia sẻ cùng tiến trình cha gần có
  thể không phân biệt được nhau — xem Open Gaps).
- **Side effects:** ghi đèn hoạt động (`{v:1, kind:'beacon', writer, writtenAt,
  windowMs, auditPid}`, thay nguyên tử) CUỐI hook, sau mọi kiểm tra từ chối, nên commit
  bị từ chối không để lại đèn. Hook KHÔNG lấy khóa `main-checkout`: đó là mutex kernel của
  writer fgOS, claim/land/approve/`fgctl init` không bao giờ đọc đèn, nên một commit ở
  main không chặn ai. Không đụng sổ đăng ký phiên, không đụng
  `sessions.lock`/`runner.lock`/mutex nóng `state`. `fgos return`/`cleanup`/`compound` xoá
  đèn của chính phiên (chỉ khi đúng writer); `fgos lock-status` hiện đèn ở trường
  `activity`.
- **Afterwards:** một commit bị từ chối in thông điệp giải thích bằng thời gian ("một
  phiên khác dường như đang hoạt động ở đây gần đây") và trỏ người tới đúng cách mở
  một cây làm việc cô lập — không bao giờ in ra một định danh thô (pid/session-id) như
  thể đó là thứ người đọc cần tự hành động theo.

oldPassage.text:
- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/locks/runner.lock` (kernel lease qua holder-lock; busy exit 6, nêu pid holder do kernel liệt kê); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); - `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/locks/runner.lock` (kernel lease qua holder-lock; busy exit 6, nêu pid holder do kernel liệt kê); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `description` là `work.description` nguyên văn, degrade "(không có)" khi vắng (per discovery-context STR30); `spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts)` nhận `opts.feedback` truyền xuống `buildPrompt`; `worktree.mjs` — lifecycle + reclaimOrphanedCheckout + `detectTrunk(repoRoot)`/`isMainWorktree(repoRoot)` (dời từ `merge.mjs` sang đây per tsk-49i — cả hai là danh tính worktree/nhánh, không mang ngữ nghĩa nội dung merge; dời đi cũng cắt luôn import vòng `merge.mjs` ↔ `worktree.mjs`) + `createBranchRef(repoRoot, id, opts)` (tạo `fgw/<id>` chỉ-là-ref, không worktree, idempotent) + `createWorktree`'s `opts.baseRef` (fork worktree mới từ một ref chỉ định thay vì HEAD hiện tại — dùng cho con fork từ tip nhánh gốc); `recovery.mjs` — 8 lớp; `anti-loop.mjs` — `visitCount` (lifetime, dùng cho outcome/metric) + `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent(events, id)` (ngân sách CỔNG, per-item, reset trên `role==='human'` mang `answer` hoặc `reason`, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)) + breaker; `loop.mjs`'s gate (cả nhánh dry-run đơn lẻ lẫn nhánh lọc `overLimit` của batch dispatch dưới) gọi `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`, không còn `visitCount`, để quyết park; `createMissBreaker` nay PER-ITEM (Map theo id, `consecutiveMissesFor(itemId)`; `consecutiveMisses` getter cũ giữ nguyên qua một khóa sentinel tương thích ngược, per fan-out-parallel-5). `runOnce`'s vòng dispatch nay là pool-loop batch (cell fan-out-parallel-8): đọc TOÀN BỘ `readyWork(dir)`, lọc qua `root-affinity.mjs`'s `steerFrontier`, nhóm theo gốc và cắt còn tối đa `parallel.maxRoots × parallel.maxLeavesPerRoot` (đọc từ `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, mặc định 4×4 khi vắng khối `parallel`), claim từng việc bên trong callback của `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (bắt buộc — giải-và-ghi phải cùng một giao dịch hàng đợi để giữ đúng chứng minh chống-tranh-giành), rồi dispatch cả mẻ đồng thời qua `Promise.allSettled`; mỗi việc claim xong xác định LEAF hay ROOT qua `state/frontier.mjs`'s `resolveRoot(view, id)` — leaf: `createBranchRef(repoRoot, rootId, {baseRef:'main'})` rồi `createWorktree(repoRoot, item.id, {worktreeDir, baseRef: branchNameFor(rootId)})`; root: `createWorktree` không đổi, tự nhiên tái dùng nhánh đã có nếu tồn tại. Mẻ xong → đọc lại `readyWork` tươi, lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng; `runOnce` trả `{outcome, dispatched, parked, reap, exitCode}` thay vì kết quả một item
- `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `parseDiscoveredBlocks(output)` + `captureDiscoveredWork(...)` — kênh báo việc-phát-hiện (xem "Báo việc-phát-hiện từ trợ lý" trên, RUL45 (báo việc-phát-hiện của trợ lý: đúng một lần mỗi lượt, fail-safe, có trần + chống trùng)): tách mọi khối lồng `fgos-discovered` (JSON, chỉ cần `title` khác rỗng) khỏi output đã thu của trợ lý, fail-safe (thân JSON hỏng/thiếu `title`/không phải object đều bị bỏ qua, không throw); gọi đúng MỘT LẦN trong `finally` bọc vòng thử lại của `dispatchClaimedItem`, tại kết cục cuối (không gọi lại giữa các lần thử nội bộ); mỗi khối hợp lệ đi qua `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (cùng cửa ghi tuần tự) — bên trong đó: cắt còn tối đa `DISCOVERY_CAP` (=20) khối trước khi lặp (phần dư log rồi bỏ), rồi với mỗi khối: quét view hiện hành tìm item có `discoveredFrom` khớp item đang thi công VÀ tên khớp sau khi chuẩn hoá (trim + hạ chữ) — khớp thì log rồi bỏ qua (không tạo); không khớp mới gọi `generateId`/`classify`/`addWork` (đóng dấu `discoveredFrom: item.id`, và stage vào-vòng của domain — `discovery` cho `coding`); `dispatch.mjs`'s văn bản prompt worker mô tả kênh khối lồng này cho trợ lý (nguyên tắc "chỉ báo, không tự ghi" — trợ lý vẫn không bao giờ được gọi `fgos`/đụng `.fgos/`); `sanitizeTitleForLog(title)` (S11, review-fix P3) — gộp khoảng trắng/xuống dòng + cắt 120 ký tự (kèm dấu `…` khi cắt), gọi tại đúng hai điểm `log` có nội suy `block.title` bên trong `captureDiscoveredWork`; KHÔNG áp dụng lên trường `title` truyền vào `addWork`
- `src/runner/goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung DUY NHẤT (`runGoalCheck(item, cwd, timeoutMs)`): chạy `item.verify` qua shell tại `cwd`, phán chỉ bằng exit status — trích xuất từ `loop.mjs` (stage-decompose S2-pull) để cả vòng tự hành LẪN cửa pull `fgos return` (spec Work-State) gọi đúng một bản logic, không bao giờ hai bản song song

- `src/intake/plan.mjs` (đổi tên từ `decompose.mjs`) — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `plan` khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc còn ở tên di sản `decompose`); verb `plan` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; `resolvePlan` cũng là chỗ nhả claim `doing→todo` khi gốc sang `executing` (claim-lock §3b)

(Helper thử-lại `src/intake/judge-executor.mjs` của bản trước đã bị xoá cùng lúc `judgeDiscovery`/`judgeDecompose` nghỉ hưu — không còn lời gọi model phán lồng nào để thử lại.)

- `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section (tsk-5vf; tsk-5hv xoá hẳn fallback về file flat legacy cũ — đây giờ là nguồn config DUY NHẤT, `fgos setup` là verb thực hiện move thật) — config committed (executor template + `modelPolicies.claude` nano/haiku, standard/sonnet, frontier/opus [tsk-5tm, thay `models` phẳng cũ; 6-tier vocab từ 2026-09-17] + timeoutMs); `executor.args` mang `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, không còn quyền git — runner commit thay worker (0052) (quyền TỐI THIỂU, xem RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp)); khối `parallel` TÙY CHỌN — `maxRoots`/`maxLeavesPerRoot` (Data Dictionary #6, mặc định trong-code 4/4 khi khối vắng mặt, mọi config cũ vẫn chạy không cần sửa); `src/runner/dispatch.mjs`'s `ensureRunnerConfigForDir(dir)` — shared-file-aware: tại đường MẶC ĐỊNH (không `--config`) vắng file, gọi `detectAssistantCli` (quét PATH thuần, không spawn — `KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES`) rồi viết `DEFAULT_RUNNER_CONFIG` với executor từ `SUPPORTED_EXECUTOR_TEMPLATES[detected]` khi trợ lý dò được có mẫu đã kiểm chứng (hôm nay chỉ `claude`, y hệt `DEFAULT_RUNNER_CONFIG.executor`), hoặc executor placeholder tự-báo-lỗi khi không (RUL48b) — rồi mới nạp, kèm một dòng thông báo tên file + executor được chọn (RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước)); `bin/fgos.mjs`'s verb `discover` và `bin/fgos-runner.mjs`'s vòng chính đều gọi `ensureRunnerConfigForDir` cho nhánh đường mặc định, `loadRunnerConfig` thẳng cho nhánh `--config` tường minh của `discover` (`fgos-runner` chỉ còn đường mặc định, RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)); đọc qua `mergeWithGlobalConfig` trước khi tách phần `runner` (project luôn thắng `~/.fgos/config.json` theo key, tsk-5vf)

- `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs` — sync base của Unit (RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first)): `seedSync` (resolve ref trước khi unit run tồn tại), `runPendingSync`, `assertSyncResumable`, `syncBrief`, `commitRoundWithSync`; git tin cậy nằm ở `commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`/`finishSyncMerge`/`syncMergeState`).

tsk-4hj `merge-blocked-other-item` — `MERGE_HEAD` đã có sẵn TRƯỚC lần merge này, thuộc về một việc KHÁC đang nhập dở, cũng là ứng viên thử lại tốt vì việc kia rồi sẽ xong hoặc bị hủy) và nhánh riêng của việc còn tồn tại (`branchExists`); đích = `branchNameFor(resolveRoot(view,id))` nếu là con, `'main'` nếu là gốc/độc lập; mở worktree ephemeral trên chính nhánh của việc, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <đích> HEAD` TRƯỚC khi nhập → nhánh đã chứa đích rồi (exit 0) → bỏ hẳn merge lẫn commit (merge sẽ là no-op, `git commit` sau đó chết vì "nothing to commit" và việc kẹt `blocked` vĩnh viễn), vẫn chạy `runGoalCheck` thật trên cây hiện có → đỏ → giữ nguyên `blocked`, KHÔNG gọi `git merge --abort` (không có merge nào đang chạy) → xanh → `moveWork(..., to:'awaiting-approval')` với `outcome: 'already-caught-up'`, không tạo commit nào; chưa chứa đích (exit 1) → `git merge --no-commit --no-ff <đích>` → xung đột thật → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; sạch → `runGoalCheck` trên cây đã stage TRƯỚC khi commit → đỏ → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; xanh → commit rồi `moveWork(..., to:'awaiting-approval', expectedStatus:'blocked')` — cạnh, không `reason`, không qua `doing` (spike `.bee/spikes/fan-out-parallel/catchup-real-conflict-probe.sh` chứng minh trước khi build cell); L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Session Identity (Writer Identity) | Foundation authority for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity` (`packages/session-identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs`. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`, route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`; Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [session-identity/spec.md](session-identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one shared vector file for Rust and Node), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; the Node leaf `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs` reads the same vectors, and reconcile imports only `facts`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`, planned); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon that also links `fgos-event-store`. Not implemented: today's Node git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them in one release per caller family. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |

Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Session Identity (Writer Identity) | Foundation authority for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity` (`packages/session-identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs`. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`, route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`; Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [session-identity/spec.md](session-identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one shared vector file for Rust and Node), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; the Node leaf `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs` reads the same vectors, and reconcile imports only `facts`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`, planned); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon that also links `fgos-event-store`. Not implemented: today's Node git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them in one release per caller family. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |

An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. It now comes from `ranConfinementBackend` (`settlement.mjs`): the prepared-invocation record the Confinement Authority published for the launch (`protected/prepared-invocation/.json`, backend type, `none` → `null`), else the attestation the dispatch returned with outcome `enforced`. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run. - **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). Work, the consumer, still does not advance on such a result: a read-only result carrying `read-only-mutation-correlated` or `mutated-dirty-before-correlated` (or, read back from disk, a non-empty `evidence.changedFiles`/`mutatedDirtyBeforeFiles`, since stored warnings are as writable as any other field) stops with its own reason `assignment--correlated-mutation` (at planning: `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`), never folded into no-evidence; a round that failed on its own terms (non-zero exit, a timeout settles as 124; a policy refusal, a proven write among them; a provider, resource or contract failure) keeps `assignment--failed`. A stored result read back without its assignment takes its mutation from its operation and recorded `role`, never from a field of its own. The executor CLI door's `stray-write-correlated` (the main checkout changed while an isolated round ran) is kept in `result.json` beside settlement's own warnings but does not stop Work: it cannot have changed the round's own checkout, and on a busy main checkout nearly every round would carry it. Dispatch keeps the warning and does not refuse the round (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` `hasReadOnlyCorrelatedMutation`; Lead decision B in `plans/261014-1400-two-doors-one-rununit/phase-00-land-finished-lanes.md`). - **RUL84 (one write-scope matcher: a Unit's `writes` has one spelling, and every "is this path in scope" question goes through `matchesWriteScope`, 2026-10-14; decision 0060).** `writes` entries are normalized once (`./`, `//`, a trailing `/` and `/.` collapse; duplicates dropped, first-seen order kept) and refused when they are `.`, empty, absolute, hold a `..` segment, a `\` or NUL, start with `:` (git pathspec magic) or glue `**` to other characters. Only `*` (inside one segment) and `**` (a whole segment, zero or more segments) are globs; every other character, `[ ] { } ! ?` included, is literal. A plain entry covers the path and everything beneath it; a glob entry must match the whole path; nothing under `.fgos/` is ever in scope, not even for `**`. One leaf module, `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` (`canonicalizeWrites`, `expandGenerated`, `matchesWriteScope`, `partitionPaths`), answers for the runner commit, settlement coverage and the Workflow out-of-scope check; git never interprets a scope. Workflow definitions use the same normalizer, and a `writes` that is not an array (YAML `writes:` left empty is `null`) is refused instead of read as `[]`. Config key `runner.generatedPaths: [{ from, also }]` (default `[]`, doctor `runner-generated-paths`): a Unit whose `writes` overlaps a generated source (`from`, e.g. `core/skills/**`) also gets that source's render trees (`also`). The widened scope is stored once in `unit.json#writeScope` when the unit run is created, never recomputed on resume, and is the `writes` of every assignment of that Unit. @@ -1117,6 +1120,7 @@ Một báo-cáo hỏng-hình (không phân tích được, thiếu tên việc) - **RUL89 (`fgos workflow start --units ` runs a list of Units as a one-off Workflow, 2026-10-14; decision 0061).** The units file (YAML/JSON, `{ id?, title?, units }` or a list of Units, `src/workflow/units-source.mjs`) becomes one step per Unit, `dependsOn` becomes step dependencies, a Unit id must be a safe branch-name segment, and the workflow id is `units/`. The `units-file` source is passed by the loader to the validator, never read from the data, and is the only source whose unit templates may carry `prefer`. `--seats` is refused with `--units`. `--effort ` (`low|medium|high|max`, otherwise refused before a run exists) becomes an override `{ reasoningEffort, origin: 'human-cli' }` for every unit, stored in `workflow.start` and reused on resume. A unit template's `persona` travels on the Unit (provenance `unit`); persona overrides remain only for `--seats` seats. A writing unit that stands on exactly one writing ancestor (directly or through read-only units; an integrate step cuts the path) starts its worktree from that unit's branch sha; a file with a writing unit standing on two or more writing units is refused at start; nothing is merged automatically and `workflow status` lists `writeBranches` (branch, worktree, base). Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared (the comparison stays needed while both inventories are read), `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare (the walk skips such an entry), `tier-fallback` warns on a family `runner.tierFallback` lists that has no cell at that tier or no agent executor. `fgos dispatch explain --for [--rigor ]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the candidates in walk order (each with the reason it is out: `tier-cell-missing`, `pool-unusable`), the walk a seat takes when each binding fails, the entries of the primary's cell (`used`, `fallback`, `unusable` with the reason), and the accounts of every pool on the walk in the order the lease takes them with whether the CLI can run on each. It leases, spawns and writes nothing. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.
