Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** @@ -3469,3 +3477,13 @@ Superseding this decision needs a new record; do not edit it in place. - **Không đóng:** transition read của `runner.providers.*.accounts` (xoá cùng khoá `runner.providers` khi mọi release trên máy đọc `runner.llmAccounts`); `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` là walker thứ hai; cổng ghi chưa nhận `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf`; trần tier theo capability và theo dõi chi phí chưa xây. - **Ranh giới:** No component-boundary change (`bind()` quyết candidate, lease quyết account). Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ. + +### D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) — một authority cho ghế agent: project thắng, tier khai trực tiếp (supersede một phần RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries)) + +- **Trạng thái:** Approved, not implemented (owner duyệt spec 2026-10-20 21:31, nguyên văn "ok, duyệt spec Seat Binding"). Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** @@ -3469,3 +3477,13 @@ Superseding this decision needs a new record; do not edit it in place. - **Không đóng:** transition read của `runner.providers.*.accounts` (xoá cùng khoá `runner.providers` khi mọi release trên máy đọc `runner.llmAccounts`); `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` là walker thứ hai; cổng ghi chưa nhận `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf`; trần tier theo capability và theo dõi chi phí chưa xây. - **Ranh giới:** No component-boundary change (`bind()` quyết candidate, lease quyết account). Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ. + +### D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) — một authority cho ghế agent: project thắng, tier khai trực tiếp (supersede một phần RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries)) + +- **Trạng thái:** Approved, not implemented (owner duyệt spec 2026-10-20 21:31, nguyên văn "ok, duyệt spec Seat Binding"). Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** @@ -3469,3 +3477,13 @@ Superseding this decision needs a new record; do not edit it in place. - **Không đóng:** transition read của `runner.providers.*.accounts` (xoá cùng khoá `runner.providers` khi mọi release trên máy đọc `runner.llmAccounts`); `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` là walker thứ hai; cổng ghi chưa nhận `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf`; trần tier theo capability và theo dõi chi phí chưa xây. - **Ranh giới:** No component-boundary change (`bind()` quyết candidate, lease quyết account). Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ. + +### D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) — một authority cho ghế agent: project thắng, tier khai trực tiếp (supersede một phần RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries)) + +- **Trạng thái:** Approved, not implemented (owner duyệt spec 2026-10-20 21:31, nguyên văn "ok, duyệt spec Seat Binding"). Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.
