currentPassage.text:
- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/locks/runner.lock` (kernel lease qua holder-lock; busy exit 6, nêu pid holder do kernel liệt kê); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. oldPassage.text:
**Architecture advisory — current boundary.** `core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md` starts registered Workflows, reads settled reports, and exposes public `workflow status`/`workflow answer` commands for the owner's declared gate; it owns no raw run-state driver or executor roster. `architecture-advisory` has five linear execution steps plus human close, with distinct panel-seat lenses and reviewed/high final synthesis; `architecture-advisory-reopen` revisits parent reports through synthesis → explanation → close without blind seats. Both synthesis templates require reviewer and red-team regardless of configured high-rigor checker defaults. Executor/provider/model/invocation selection remains config + `bind()` owned. Required read-only posture refuses unsafe execution.
`council-lite` is a one-panel discussion Workflow: `params.roleTasks` gives each seat one task posture from `core/agents/council-*.yaml`, supplied through template `contextRefs`. Each description contains method, blind spot, and an explicit evidence-led ending rule; posture is not actor identity, registry membership, or provider policy. `bind()` spreads seats across provider families as a preference (decision 0055), never refusing a seat for sharing one. No runtime or renderer seam is added. Each seat first writes a short "Restatement" of the question and what it treats as out of scope before analysing, and the synthesizer lists mismatched restatements as unresolved evidence.
`workflow start --seats "<lens>|<lens>|..."` rebuilds a registered base whose panels are generic (`group-cognition`, `business-discussion`, `nominal-group`, `delphi`) with one panel seat per lens (decision 0056). A panel unit is generic when its `params.roleTasks` has no `panelist-N` key and it sets no custom `params.role`; a base with no generic panel, or with any curated one (`council-lite`, `architecture-advisory`), is refused with the reason, so lenses never overwrite curated seats. The Workflow component (`src/workflow/seats.mjs`, called from `prepareWorkflowRun`) clones the loaded base and, on every generic panel unit, sets `params.members = N` and `roleTasks.panelist-1..N` from one runtime-owned sentence that frames the lens as a task focus and ends in `{objective}`; Delphi gets the same seats in both rounds so `sameSeat` inputs stay aligned. Steps, `dependsOn`, gates, `blind`, checker and synthesizer text are untouched and the result is revalidated by the same validator. Entries: at least 2, no schema maximum, distinct case-insensitively; a lens is 3-160 characters on one line without braces or `|`; an entry `@name` (`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}` after the `@`) seats a named persona on that panel seat alone (decision 0057). Run-level `--context-ref` reaches only root steps, so with `--seats` the shared refs are also copied into the template of every unit in a step that depends on another. Before the run is recorded the CLI dry-binds the expanded panel units (`preflightWorkflowSeats`, `simulateUnitBindings`): seats that would share a provider family are returned as `seatsPreflight.warnings` (informational), and a role no candidate can serve refuses the start; nothing is created in either case. The expanded definition is stored in the existing `workflow.start` event with a provenance record `seats: { seats, baseId, baseDigest, refs }` and the status projection exposes `seats`; resume and status read stored data and never re-expand, and `workflow resume --seats` refuses seats that differ from the stored ones. Without `--seats` the definition, event and projection are unchanged.
A named persona is looked up once by `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs`: workspace `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` of the working project, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/` (a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the installed package's), whole-file replacement across tiers, two files of one name in one tier is an error, an unknown name is an error that lists every folder searched, and a file must declare `name:` equal to its basename and a non-empty `description:`. `prepareWorkflowRun` resolves every name before the run exists and records `seats.personas: [{ seat, name, tier, source, digest, text }]` (the exact file bytes and their SHA-256) in the same `workflow.start` event; the status projection exposes it. The runner emits, for every panel unit, one override `{ scope: { unit, role: "panelist-N" }, persona, personaPin, origin: "workflow" }` per named seat ahead of the unit-wide persona override, so `bind()` (first matching override, unchanged) gives the persona to that seat only; the synthesizer and checkers never inherit it. `run.mjs` copies the pin of the matching override onto the assignment's `policy.personaPin`, and `renderPersonaSection` renders the pinned text through the same parser instead of reading a file, so resume and later steps never re-read the live file. A lens seat keeps the runtime lens sentence; a named seat has no lens task and keeps the unit's objective as its task.
Reviewed templates alone may declare `acceptOutcomes: [pass, findings]`; omission remains pass-only. Evidenced `done`/`findings` retains completed execution and findings on both read-only and mutating settlement branches; this does not imply approval or permission to advance mutating work. Coding feature validation and implementation retain revision followed by step failure if findings remain. Business discussion, group cognition, advisory critique/synthesis and marketing draft-copy opt in explicitly; marketing still parks for human approval. Findings never excuse transport/execution failure.
The coding driver honors an explicit operation-choice repair route or canProceed before the generic satisfied gate; explicit stop still wins. Thus review REJECT/findings routes to fix-verify-red, while plan NOT READY/findings stays on the planning path. Mutating producer findings leaves dirty work uncommitted. Claude herdr grants only the current run, copied inputs and canonical parent directories of existing absolute file contextRefs; this is prompt-policy preparation, not expanded OS confinement or live proof.
Repeatable `workflow start --context-ref <ref>` uses the template validator and persists one `contextRefs` field in the start event/projection, delivered to every Unit in a root step; template refs remain local to their owning Unit. Cross-repo launches reject plain paths before run creation: use state-root `unit-run:<id>/<role>` or `gate-answer:<run>/<step>` refs. Linked worktrees of the same repository retain plain-path support. No extra capture/provenance state is introduced.
The final producer report must be a RAW JSON object with `"missing expertise": []` or nonblank string entries. The new `{{report:synthesis/synthesize-recommendation:missing expertise}}` reference in a human `gate.question` reads the settled, hash-verified producer report and renders the fixed batched close. The field is read under either spelling (`missing expertise` or `missing_expertise`); when the report itself is prose, a `packet-*.json` object beside it counts only if it was not modified after the report settled, because the report digest does not cover it. Fenced or prose-embedded JSON is never parsed. Malformed or absent reports park with a clear error and no inferred expertise; resume remains parked, and the owner may answer after manual review with an acknowledged limitation.

Each description contains method, blind spot, and an explicit evidence-led ending rule; posture is not actor identity, registry membership, or provider policy. `bind()` spreads seats across provider families as a preference (decision 0055), never refusing a seat for sharing one. No runtime or renderer seam is added. Each seat first writes a short "Restatement" of the question and what it treats as out of scope before analysing, and the synthesizer lists mismatched restatements as unresolved evidence.
`workflow start --seats "<lens>|<lens>|..."` rebuilds a registered base whose panels are generic (`group-cognition`, `business-discussion`, `nominal-group`, `delphi`) with one panel seat per lens (decision 0056). A panel unit is generic when its `params.roleTasks` has no `panelist-N` key and it sets no custom `params.role`; a base with no generic panel, or with any curated one (`council-lite`, `architecture-advisory`), is refused with the reason, so lenses never overwrite curated seats. The Workflow component (`src/workflow/seats.mjs`, called from `prepareWorkflowRun`) clones the loaded base and, on every generic panel unit, sets `params.members = N` and `roleTasks.panelist-1..N` from one runtime-owned sentence that frames the lens as a task focus and ends in `{objective}`; Delphi gets the same seats in both rounds so `sameSeat` inputs stay aligned. Steps, `dependsOn`, gates, `blind`, checker and synthesizer text are untouched and the result is revalidated by the same validator. Entries: at least 2, no schema maximum, distinct case-insensitively; a lens is 3-160 characters on one line without braces or `|`; an entry `@name` (`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}` after the `@`) seats a named persona on that panel seat alone (decision 0057). Run-level `--context-ref` reaches only root steps, so with `--seats` the shared refs are also copied into the template of every unit in a step that depends on another. Before the run is recorded the CLI dry-binds the expanded panel units (`preflightWorkflowSeats`, `simulateUnitBindings`): seats that would share a provider family are returned as `seatsPreflight.warnings` (informational), and a role no candidate can serve refuses the start; nothing is created in either case. The expanded definition is stored in the existing `workflow.start` event with a provenance record `seats: { seats, baseId, baseDigest, refs }` and the status projection exposes `seats`; resume and status read stored data and never re-expand, and `workflow resume --seats` refuses seats that differ from the stored ones. Without `--seats` the definition, event and projection are unchanged.
A named persona is looked up once by `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs`: workspace `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` of the working project, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/` (a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the installed package's), whole-file replacement across tiers, two files of one name in one tier is an error, an unknown name is an error that lists every folder searched, and a file must declare `name:` equal to its basename and a non-empty `description:`. `prepareWorkflowRun` resolves every name before the run exists and records `seats.personas: [{ seat, name, tier, source, digest, text }]` (the exact file bytes and their SHA-256) in the same `workflow.start` event; the status projection exposes it. The runner emits, for every panel unit, one override `{ scope: { unit, role: "panelist-N" }, persona, personaPin, origin: "workflow" }` per named seat ahead of the unit-wide persona override, so `bind()` (first matching override, unchanged) gives the persona to that seat only; the synthesizer and checkers never inherit it. `run.mjs` copies the pin of the matching override onto the assignment's `policy.personaPin`, and `renderPersonaSection` renders the pinned text through the same parser instead of reading a file, so resume and later steps never re-read the live file. A lens seat keeps the runtime lens sentence; a named seat has no lens task and keeps the unit's objective as its task.
Reviewed templates alone may declare `acceptOutcomes: [pass, findings]`; omission remains pass-only. Evidenced `done`/`findings` retains completed execution and findings on both read-only and mutating settlement branches; this does not imply approval or permission to advance mutating work. Coding feature validation and implementation retain revision followed by step failure if findings remain. Business discussion, group cognition, advisory critique/synthesis and marketing draft-copy opt in explicitly; marketing still parks for human approval. Findings never excuse transport/execution failure.
The coding driver honors an explicit operation-choice repair route or canProceed before the generic satisfied gate; explicit stop still wins. Thus review REJECT/findings routes to fix-verify-red, while plan NOT READY/findings stays on the planning path. Mutating producer findings leaves dirty work uncommitted. Claude herdr grants only the current run, copied inputs and canonical parent directories of existing absolute file contextRefs; this is prompt-policy preparation, not expanded OS confinement or live proof.
Repeatable `workflow start --context-ref <ref>` uses the template validator and persists one `contextRefs` field in the start event/projection, delivered to every Unit in a root step; template refs remain local to their owning Unit. Cross-repo launches reject plain paths before run creation: use state-root `unit-run:<id>/<role>` or `gate-answer:<run>/<step>` refs. Linked worktrees of the same repository retain plain-path support. No extra capture/provenance state is introduced.
The final producer report must be a RAW JSON object with `"missing expertise": []` or nonblank string entries. The new `{{report:synthesis/synthesize-recommendation:missing expertise}}` reference in a human `gate.question` reads the settled, hash-verified producer report and renders the fixed batched close. The field is read under either spelling (`missing expertise` or `missing_expertise`); when the report itself is prose, a `packet-*.json` object beside it counts only if it was not modified after the report settled, because the report digest does not cover it. Fenced or prose-embedded JSON is never parsed. Malformed or absent reports park with a clear error and no inferred expertise; resume remains parked, and the owner may answer after manual review with an acknowledged limitation.

Một cờ ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow): `blind: true` làm *mọi vai* của Unit chạy với `hostRead: blind` (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §9.2): worker không đọc được `.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs` của project, thư mục socket herdr, private home của dispatch khác, hay `/proc/<pid>` của tiến trình anh em; chỉ đọc được thư mục của chính nó (brief, ref đã được trao — chỉ-đọc) và ghi outbox. Phần còn lại của host (repo, `node`, DNS) và file tracked trong `.fgos` không đổi. Unit `blind` không bao giờ chạy không-blind: nếu không thực thi được — `bind()` không chọn in-process/inline, không có bwrap, mode không `required`, probe hỏng/chưa tươi, `cwd` hay ref nằm trong vùng bị che — dispatch bị từ chối trước khi spawn với lý do có tên (`blind-in-process`, `blind-requires-confinement`, `blind-hides-workspace`, `blind-ref-hidden`, `confinement-probe-failed`, ...). Với Unit `blind`, input `unit-run:`/`gate-answer:` (và ref bất kỳ nằm trong vùng bị che) không được giao bằng đường dẫn gốc: lúc dispatch, `resolveUnitInputs` + `copyHandoffsInto` chép nguyên byte (kiểm sha256) vào `inputs/` của round dir của chính vai đó, mỗi vai một bản, tên trung tính khi có `anonymizeInputs`; `unit.json` giữ `inputMap`, resume dùng lại bản chép. `blind-ref-hidden` chỉ còn cho ref không chép được. Workflow bật `blind`: hai bước panel của `delphi` (`propose-round-1`, `propose-round-2`), `generate-ideas` của `nominal-group`, `sense-making-panel` của `group-cognition`, `shaping` của `architecture-advisory` (`core/workflows/architecture-advisory.yaml`) và `perspectives` của `business-discussion` (`core/workflows/business-discussion.yaml`).

An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. It now comes from `ranConfinementBackend` (`settlement.mjs`): the prepared-invocation record the Confinement Authority published for the launch (`protected/prepared-invocation/.json`, backend type, `none` → `null`), else the attestation the dispatch returned with outcome `enforced`. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run. - **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). oldPassage.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled (Request-to-Run P1 Execution Core hoàn tất, 2026-10-01)
- **Bối cảnh:** L5 trước P1 bị phân mảnh: "ai làm" bị quyết định ở nhiều nơi (coordination engine, `decide`, placement-policy, `assignment-policy.mjs`); "chạy qua cửa nào" có nhiều cửa ad-hoc; read-only bị chia rẽ giữa invocation `*-readonly` và tool gating; cổng ghi file phụ thuộc template stamp của engine.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Hợp đồng Unit (`src/runner/execution/unit.mjs`):** Hợp đồng dữ liệu duy nhất cho mọi đường vào. Phi hạ tầng (G2) — cấm chứa executor/provider/model/tier/invocation/actors/prefer/overrides.
  2. **Một `bind()` duy nhất (`src/runner/execution/bind.mjs`):** Bảng 5 mức (Session -> Overrides -> Unit role/rigor -> Project taste -> Global taste), tái dùng `mechanism.mjs` theo D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch).
  3. **Một cửa chạy `fgos run` (`src/runner/execution/run.mjs`):** Bọc `executeAssignment`, mặc định spawn qua pane herdr (G7), cli fallback. Có `fgos run record` cho producer inline với nonce một lần phát kèm chỉ dẫn và kiểm chứng `evidenceRefs`.
  4. **3 Pattern cộng tác (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`):** Vòng lặp code nhỏ, thuần, không store mới (Q-B: trạng thái vòng lặp suy từ `history()` của Unit run). `findings` là outcome, không đánh `failed`.
  5. **Cổng ghi file kiểm chứng được (supersede ADR-006 §6):** Assignment `mutating` được admit khi: (a) cwd là linked worktree và `realpath(cwd) == unit.json.worktree`, (b) `bind()` tính lại từ `unit.json` khớp deep-equal. Ngoại lệ có tên: engine protocol stamp giữ tới P4 phase 6. D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch) giữ nguyên.
  6. **Xoá bỏ hoàn toàn:** Invocations `*-readonly`, `readOnlyRedirects`, `placement-policy.mjs`. `executors.*.for` và PolicyPatch `preferExecutor`/`preferPersona` vẫn được lớp dispatch đọc tại `src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`) và `src/runner/dispatch/assignment-policy.mjs`; không phải các trường đã xoá. Đường Execution Core chọn executor qua `bind()` với overrides và `capabilities.*.prefer` (`src/runner/execution/bind.mjs`). Posture read-only/ghi file là confinement OS do fgOS áp cho cả herdr lẫn cli (X-1). Quota limit `provider-limit` kích hoạt `bind().nextCandidate` mở pane mới giữ pane cũ (X-3).
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** @@ -3469,3 +3477,13 @@ Superseding this decision needs a new record; do not edit it in place. - **Không đóng:** transition read của `runner.providers.*.accounts` (xoá cùng khoá `runner.providers` khi mọi release trên máy đọc `runner.llmAccounts`); `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` là walker thứ hai; cổng ghi chưa nhận `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf`; trần tier theo capability và theo dõi chi phí chưa xây. - **Ranh giới:** No component-boundary change (`bind()` quyết candidate, lease quyết account). Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ. + +### D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) — một authority cho ghế agent: project thắng, tier khai trực tiếp (supersede một phần RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries)) + +- **Trạng thái:** Approved, not implemented (owner duyệt spec 2026-10-20 21:31, nguyên văn "ok, duyệt spec Seat Binding"). Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

oldPassage.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled (Request-to-Run P2 Runnable Plans hoàn tất, 2026-10-01)
- **Bối cảnh:** Trước P2, việc phân rã và chọn capability/cơ chế bị phân mảnh bởi lớp prose L2 DemandFacts (8 fields) -> matcher -> `form` (`inline|protocol|facade`). Các facade `fgos-code-change`, `fgos-code-panel`, `fgos-plan-loop` tự lập lịch, tự chạy vòng lặp bằng prose, tạo ra nhiều sequencer chồng chéo và gắn chặt vào domain coding.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Unit là hợp đồng dữ liệu duy nhất (`src/runner/execution/unit.mjs`):** Mọi đường vào (prompt tự do, plan AgentKit, phase file) đều quy về Unit. `fgos plan-lint` kiểm chứng Unit trong phase file (`## Units`, `- unit:`), phát hiện sớm ghim hạ tầng (G2), trùng id, vòng phụ thuộc, và giao nhau `writes` không có `dependsOn`.
  2. **Driver mỏng (`core/skills/fgos-run`):** Thay thế toàn bộ các facade cũ (`fgos-code-change`, `fgos-code-panel`, `fgos-plan-loop`, `fgos-capability-dispatching`). Driver không tự lập lịch, không tự merge mà giao trọn cho **Workflow runner** (`src/workflow/runner.mjs`, P3a).
  3. **Cổng người thống nhất:** Authorize không parse từ prose plan. Phase chưa được duyệt sẽ dừng ở cổng người của Workflow run (`gate: { kind: "human" }`), owner trả lời qua `fgos workflow answer`. Mọi câu hỏi treo được gom thành một bộ duy nhất. Mọi cổng người mặc định là consent gate (`mode: "consent"`, fail-closed): chỉ nhả runner khi trả lời kèm `--approve`; trả lời không có `--approve` là lời làm rõ (clarification note) và gate giữ nguyên `parked`. Cổng nào chủ động khai `mode: "input"` thì câu trả lời nội dung là đủ để tiến bước.
  4. **Xoá bỏ DemandFacts & matcher:** Xoá `src/runner/capability-match.mjs`, verb `fgos capability match`, các fragment `capability-matching.md`. L2 chỉ còn hiểu yêu cầu và viết Unit với `capability` (`domain:verb`).
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared (the comparison stays needed while both inventories are read), `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare (the walk skips such an entry), `tier-fallback` warns on a family `runner.tierFallback` lists that has no cell at that tier or no agent executor. `fgos dispatch explain --for [--rigor ]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the candidates in walk order (each with the reason it is out: `tier-cell-missing`, `pool-unusable`), the walk a seat takes when each binding fails, the entries of the primary's cell (`used`, `fallback`, `unusable` with the reason), and the accounts of every pool on the walk in the order the lease takes them with whether the CLI can run on each. It leases, spawns and writes nothing. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). + - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** @@ -3469,3 +3477,13 @@ Superseding this decision needs a new record; do not edit it in place. - **Không đóng:** transition read của `runner.providers.*.accounts` (xoá cùng khoá `runner.providers` khi mọi release trên máy đọc `runner.llmAccounts`); `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` là walker thứ hai; cổng ghi chưa nhận `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf`; trần tier theo capability và theo dõi chi phí chưa xây. - **Ranh giới:** No component-boundary change (`bind()` quyết candidate, lease quyết account). Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ. + +### D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) — một authority cho ghế agent: project thắng, tier khai trực tiếp (supersede một phần RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries)) + +- **Trạng thái:** Approved, not implemented (owner duyệt spec 2026-10-20 21:31, nguyên văn "ok, duyệt spec Seat Binding"). Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

oldPassage.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled (2026-10-05)
- **Bối cảnh:** Có hai đường truyền kết quả. Giữa các vai trong một Unit run là đường dẫn trong `contextRefs`; giữa các bước Workflow là text nhúng vào objective, tối đa 6000 ký tự của report cuối mỗi unit, tìm report bằng tên file (`agent-report.md`) nên bỏ sót `report-N.md` của herdr, và chỉ giữ kết quả cuối nên một bước `panel` chỉ còn synthesizer. Ref `unit-run:<id>/<role>` được validate nhưng không bao giờ phân giải, worker nhận một chuỗi không phải đường dẫn. Store của Workflow không giữ unit run id nên không dựng được ref.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Một dạng:** đường dẫn tuyệt đối, chỉ đọc, tới report, trong `contextRefs`; không còn đường nhúng text. Xoá giới hạn 6000 ký tự, tìm report theo tên file và `role-input-refs.mjs`.
  2. **Một chỗ phân giải** trong Execution Core (`handoff-refs.mjs`), lúc tạo Unit run, kết quả ghi vào `unit.json` (`resolvedInputs`). Report lấy từ `settleReports` (đã kiểm sha256), không đoán theo tên file.
  3. **Workflow store ghi `unitRunId`** ngay khi Unit run được tạo (event `unit.started`, trước ghế đầu tiên) và lặp lại trên `unit.complete`; một unit đang `running` có id được runner tiếp tục bằng `resumeUnitRunId` (ghế đã settle không chạy lại, worktree đã ghi được dùng lại) thay vì tạo Unit run mới; bước sau thấy report của mọi vai của mọi bước phụ thuộc, như trước.
  4. Không mở rộng quyền đọc của worker (xem "Ranh giới tin cậy" ở `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md`); không đổi ranh giới component.
- **Giới hạn đã biết:** worker phải mở file; câu `Summary` giữ trong objective làm sàn khi một model bỏ qua ref. Câu trả lời của cổng người chưa tới unit sau.
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

- **Trạng thái:** Settled (2026-10-05)
- **Bối cảnh:** Có hai đường truyền kết quả. Giữa các vai trong một Unit run là đường dẫn trong `contextRefs`; giữa các bước Workflow là text nhúng vào objective, tối đa 6000 ký tự của report cuối mỗi unit, tìm report bằng tên file (`agent-report.md`) nên bỏ sót `report-N.md` của herdr, và chỉ giữ kết quả cuối nên một bước `panel` chỉ còn synthesizer. Ref `unit-run:<id>/<role>` được validate nhưng không bao giờ phân giải, worker nhận một chuỗi không phải đường dẫn. Store của Workflow không giữ unit run id nên không dựng được ref.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Một dạng:** đường dẫn tuyệt đối, chỉ đọc, tới report, trong `contextRefs`; không còn đường nhúng text. Xoá giới hạn 6000 ký tự, tìm report theo tên file và `role-input-refs.mjs`.
  2. **Một chỗ phân giải** trong Execution Core (`handoff-refs.mjs`), lúc tạo Unit run, kết quả ghi vào `unit.json` (`resolvedInputs`). Report lấy từ `settleReports` (đã kiểm sha256), không đoán theo tên file.
  3. **Workflow store ghi `unitRunId`** ngay khi Unit run được tạo (event `unit.started`, trước ghế đầu tiên) và lặp lại trên `unit.complete`; một unit đang `running` có id được runner tiếp tục bằng `resumeUnitRunId` (ghế đã settle không chạy lại, worktree đã ghi được dùng lại) thay vì tạo Unit run mới; bước sau thấy report của mọi vai của mọi bước phụ thuộc, như trước.
  4. Không mở rộng quyền đọc của worker (xem "Ranh giới tin cậy" ở `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md`); không đổi ranh giới component.
- **Giới hạn đã biết:** worker phải mở file; câu `Summary` giữ trong objective làm sàn khi một model bỏ qua ref. Câu trả lời của cổng người chưa tới unit sau.
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home.
