A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run. - **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). Work, the consumer, still does not advance on such a result: a read-only result carrying `read-only-mutation-correlated` or `mutated-dirty-before-correlated` (or, read back from disk, a non-empty `evidence.changedFiles`/`mutatedDirtyBeforeFiles`, since stored warnings are as writable as any other field) stops with its own reason `assignment--correlated-mutation` (at planning: `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`), never folded into no-evidence; a round that failed on its own terms (non-zero exit, a timeout settles as 124; a policy refusal, a proven write among them; a provider, resource or contract failure) keeps `assignment--failed`. A stored result read back without its assignment takes its mutation from its operation and recorded `role`, never from a field of its own. The executor CLI door's `stray-write-correlated` (the main checkout changed while an isolated round ran) is kept in `result.json` beside settlement's own warnings but does not stop Work: it cannot have changed the round's own checkout, and on a busy main checkout nearly every round would carry it. Dispatch keeps the warning and does not refuse the round (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` `hasReadOnlyCorrelatedMutation`; Lead decision B in `plans/261014-1400-two-doors-one-rununit/phase-00-land-finished-lanes.md`). - **RUL84 (one write-scope matcher: a Unit's `writes` has one spelling, and every "is this path in scope" question goes through `matchesWriteScope`, 2026-10-14; decision 0060).** `writes` entries are normalized once (`./`, `//`, a trailing `/` and `/.` collapse; duplicates dropped, first-seen order kept) and refused when they are `.`, empty, absolute, hold a `..` segment, a `\` or NUL, start with `:` (git pathspec magic) or glue `**` to other characters. Only `*` (inside one segment) and `**` (a whole segment, zero or more segments) are globs; every other character, `[ ] { } ! ?` included, is literal. A plain entry covers the path and everything beneath it; a glob entry must match the whole path; nothing under `.fgos/` is ever in scope, not even for `**`. One leaf module, `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` (`canonicalizeWrites`, `expandGenerated`, `matchesWriteScope`, `partitionPaths`), answers for the runner commit, settlement coverage and the Workflow out-of-scope check; git never interprets a scope.   1. **Transport do `bind()` quyết, `run.mjs` đọc.** herdr khi herdr có mặt trong session **và** executor có invocation `herdr-spawn` có id mà `canApplyPosture` chấp nhận; ngược lại cli (lý do ghi ở `provenance.transport.source`). Transport và invocation thật nằm trong `assignment.json` / `unit.json`, không chỉ ở giá trị trả về. Executor có CLI vẫn out-of-process (D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch, executor có CLI luôn chạy ngoài process)).
  2. **Posture một đường.** `resolvePosture` chỉ ánh xạ posture -> `requirement` (policy built-in); `requirement` đi vào `buildConfinementRequest` -> Confinement Authority -> driver bwrap, cho cả pane herdr lẫn cli. Không còn `bwrapArgs` tự dựng trong `policies.mjs` (guard test). `resolvePostureInvocation` (`canApplyPosture` là dạng boolean của nó) là nơi duy nhất quyết: invocation khai `confinement.backend`, backend bật trong registry máy, executable chạy được; thiếu thì bind lọc candidate hoặc từ chối `posture-unavailable`, không chạy không confine. Nó cũng trả về invocation đã duyệt: khi `prefer` không nêu invocation, bind ghi đúng invocation cli thường đầu tiên mang được posture (không phải invocation cli đầu tiên của executor; `herdr-spawn` chỉ tính khi session ở trong herdr) vào binding, và `run.mjs` ghim đúng nó. Entry `prefer` nêu invocation thì giữ nguyên. Nên mọi invocation muốn được chọn phải khai `confinement`, và invocation của agent ghi state ngoài thư mục chỉ-đọc (codex, agy, pi) phải khai thêm `resourceBindings` private-home.
  5. **Tra capability.** `bind()` tìm `capabilities[domain:verb]` trước, rồi `capabilities[verb]`, nhưng entry chỉ thắng khi có `prefer` dùng được: slot chỉ có `description` (loại `fgos setup` ghi) không che bare-verb có `prefer`. Không có `prefer` ở đâu cả thì headless bị từ chối `headless-no-executor`; `fgos doctor` (`workflow-capabilities-configured`) cảnh báo đúng capability đó. Mặc định headless chỉ chạy được với Workflow đã khai `prefer`, không phải mọi Workflow `fgos setup` đã ghi slot.
  3. **Fallback quota.** `provider-limit` (herdr đọc màn hình qua detector của herdr, mặc định idle 5 phút nếu config không đặt `idleTimeoutMs`) -> `nextCandidate` đi tiếp `prefer[]` -> pane mới dưới assignment id `<unitRun>/<role>/<round>-fb<n>`; pane cũ giữ nguyên; `fallbackFrom` ghi lại; hết candidate thì outcome vẫn `provider-limit`. cli-spawn không có phát hiện limit nên headless không fallback (*cập nhật 2026-10-14:* nay có, qua câu hạn mức ở đuôi stderr, xem đoạn decision 0058 ở RUL65b). Pane idle (không `working`) quá 15 giây bị đọc màn hình để tìm credential chết (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, vd pi "OAuth refresh failed ... invalid_grant"): thấy thì cũng kết thúc `provider-limit` ngay, không chờ idle timeout, để walk sang candidate kế; classifier ghi quarantine `auth-token` kiểu `manual-clear` (tới khi người login lại và `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine`), không phải `quota-limit`. Quarantine quota dùng đúng thời gian reset provider ghi trên màn hình ("Resets in 24m1s", cả giờ/phút/giây), mặc định 1 giờ khi không ghi.
  4. **Pane confine cho cả năm họ** (claude, claude qua OpenRouter, codex, agy, pi): mỗi agent giữ state trong private home dựng từ account được lease; công thức và lý do ở [confinement-authority.md §13.1](./confinement-authority.md), account inventory toàn máy ở RUL65b (trên).
  - **Pane không nhận HOME riêng của worker.** Vòng herdr confine mở pane không kèm `HOME` private (launcher script tự `export` nó trước khi `exec`): shell của pane mà bắt đầu trong một home không có file khởi động thì zsh chạy trình hướng dẫn lần đầu và nuốt lệnh khởi chạy gõ ngay sau, nên vòng agy báo `foreground process ... does not match prepared command argv` dù argv không sai.
  - **Prompt delivery trong pane herdr (`inline` mặc định, `file-pointer` tuỳ chọn).** Mặc định `herdr-spawn` gửi toàn bộ nội dung `brief-<round>.md` trực tiếp vào pane qua `herdr agent prompt` (bracketed paste) để người quan sát thấy trọn vẹn prompt trong TUI, đồng thời vẫn ghi `brief-<round>.md` xuống đĩa kèm dòng trỏ đường dẫn phục hồi sau compaction; `promptDelivery: "file-pointer"` (hoặc `FGOS_HERDR_PROMPT_DELIVERY=file-pointer`) giữ cơ chế gõ con trỏ một dòng. `confirmBriefSubmitted` nhận diện cả paste chip thu gọn (`[Pasted text #1 +N lines]`, `[paste #1 +N lines]`, `[Paste]`, `#1 … +N lines`, menu `Pasted N lines`) ở vùng composer cuối màn hình; `SHELL_MANAGED_ENV` giữ nguyên `TERM`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` của pane mới (không để `TERM=dumb` hay `HERDR_PANE_ID` của process gọi ghi đè), `workerBaseEnv` loại bỏ `OMPCODE`/`OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_PROFILE`/`PI_CONFIG_FILES` của phiên cha, và `executors.xai` có thêm invocation `omp-herdr-vantt` chạy `omp` trong pane `bwrap`.
- **Bằng chứng:** [acceptance-herdr.md](../../plans/261002-1339-request-to-run-p6-herdr-posture-quota/reports/acceptance-herdr.md): ca 1 (Unit `reviewed`), 2 (reviewer bị chặn ghi repo, ghi được outbox), 3 (Workflow `architecture-advisory` 9 role trong pane, 4 họ provider), 4 (fallback, pane cũ giữ), 6 (headless cli cùng posture) Accepted; transport đọc từ `assignment.json`.
- **Giới hạn đã biết:**
  - Ca 5 (so cùng câu hỏi với engine cũ, tag `pre-engine-retirement`) **NOT RUN**: engine cũ cần Lead tự viết và authorize từng bước, nên "Lead-active" sẽ đo chính thao tác tay, không đo engine.
  - Ca 4 dùng màn hình limit **giả** (executor `fake-limit`); `DEFAULT_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` chưa đo trên màn hình limit thật của claude/codex. *Cập nhật 2026-10-05:* câu chữ đo được đầu tiên là của codex, "■ Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model." (đã thêm vào mẫu mặc định). Ngoài ra, thang liveness chỉ đọc màn hình khi tiến độ dừng, mà `working` tính là tiến độ, nên pane vẫn báo `working` nhưng đang kẹt ở lỗi nhà cung cấp chạy tới trần 15 phút không fallback (thấy khi dogfood mdview). Nay vòng thăm dò đọc 15 dòng cuối của agent đang `working` mỗi 30 giây và kết luận `provider-limit` khi cùng một dòng bắt đầu bằng dấu lỗi của CLI (`■`) và nêu điều kiện (`WORKING_STALL_PATTERNS`, chỉ câu chữ đã đo) còn nằm đó sau một khoảng thăm dò đầy đủ; chữ thường nhắc tới capacity hay rate limit không bị đụng tới.
  - **Trạng thái agent trong herdr (đo 2026-10-05, herdr 0.9.1-vantt.1).** herdr có đúng một nguồn trạng thái cho mỗi pane; fgos từng `pane report-agent --state working` lúc khởi động pane bị cô lập, nên fgos thành nguồn đó và `agent get` đứng yên ở `working` cả vòng (commit `2e9b53f6c` chỉ là đường vòng: đọc `agent explain` trước, hai lần gọi herdr mỗi nhịp thăm dò). Thí nghiệm trong pane thật: claude, codex, agy, pi chạy sau bwrap (không tách pid namespace) đều được herdr nhận ra không cần `HERDR_AGENT`, `agent get` khớp `agent explain`, và `agent prompt --wait` trả `done` sau ~2 giây; sau khi fgos báo `working`, `agent get` kẹt `working` còn `explain` nói `idle`, `agent prompt --wait` quá thời gian; `pane release-agent` trả lại quyền, trạng thái hồi phục sau vài giây. Nay fgos không báo trạng thái; chỉ khi herdr không nhận ra tiến trình là agent (sau 6 giây) mới báo, vì đó là cách duy nhất đánh địa chỉ nó (`ensureHerdrKnowsAgent`). Vòng thăm dò đọc `agent get`, chỉ hỏi `explain` khi `unknown`. Giới hạn: herdr chỉ biết `idle/working/blocked/done/unknown`, không biết lý do; manifest codex khớp ký tự xoay trong tiêu đề terminal là `working` (rule `osc_title_working`), nên pane codex kẹt ở lỗi nhà cung cấp vẫn là `working` và vẫn cần phần đọc màn hình ở trên. Mỗi vòng không bình thường để lại `herdr-diagnosis.json` (lời giải thích của chính herdr).
  - **Agent kẹt ở prompt chỉ người trả lời được (đo 2026-10-05, codex "Trust this folder?").** herdr báo đúng `blocked` (luật `trust_directory`), thang liveness kết luận `blocked` kèm dòng màn hình, nhưng bước settle coi mọi lỗi mang lớp `worker-timeout` là timeout nên run ghi `execution-timeout` và Unit ra `execution-failure`. Nay `blocked` (như `provider-limit`) đi thẳng qua `adapterOutcome`: `failure.code = blocked`, `outcome.category = blocked`, Unit outcome `blocked`, pane giữ nguyên, thông báo nêu cách sửa (trả lời prompt hoặc cấp trust cho project trong home của agent). Không thêm mẫu màn hình vì detector của herdr đã nhận ra màn hình này; màn hình không đọc được vẫn không phải bằng chứng.
  - Inventory account (`runner.providers.<provider>.accounts`) chỉ ở `~/.fgos/config.json` toàn máy; mỗi máy phải tự khai, `fgos setup` không tạo; `fgos doctor` (`confined-pane-accounts`) đọc inventory từ config toàn máy bất kể cwd (không cần project config) và chỉ ra pane thiếu entry; config toàn máy không đọc được thì check FAIL, nêu mã lỗi và đường dẫn.
  - bind chọn invocation herdr **đầu tiên** của executor; executor nhiều account cần luật chọn tường minh về sau.
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. - **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `src/state/**`, `src/workflow/**` hay bất kỳ module tầng Work (`work-compat`, `work-dispatch`, `operation-choice`, `loop`, `claim-port`, `prompt-templates`, `intake/`, `verbs/`), và không chứa literal tên domain/bước (guard `test/architecture.test.mjs`, tên đọc từ `domains/*/` trên đĩa). Cụ thể:
  1. Operation/taskSpec/skill của một bước đến từ định nghĩa Workflow (`domains/<d>/workflows/*.yaml`, `steps[].operations`/`skill`), tầng Work đọc qua `src/state/domain-registry.mjs` rồi đưa vào `buildAssignment({ domain, stage, operation, operations })`. Dispatch kiểm `operation ∈ operations` (lỗi `unknown operation ... for stage ...`), ghi danh sách hợp lệ vào `provenance.declared.legalOperations`; `executeAssignment` từ chối một Assignment declared không mang danh sách đó hoặc có `operation` ngoài danh sách (và `dispatch: human-only`). Trường `stage` trên Assignment hiện chỉ còn là nhãn mờ của bước (đổi tên theo đợt thuật ngữ).
  2. [Phần đầu vào còn lại ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only) — `work`/`workItem`/`workExecutorId` thôi là đầu vào của dispatch; `decide --work` nhận hint; `workDispatchContext` không còn trả `work`] Mọi thứ Work-aware chuyển ra tầng Work: `src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` (chọn operation cho bước hiện tại, trước ở `dispatch/`), `src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs` (`spawnWorker`, `resolveAgentTypeForWork`, `resolveWorkForDispatch`, `workDispatchContext`), `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (`executorIdForWork`, `buildPrompt`, `workCapabilityHints`). Dispatch nhận đầu vào đã phân giải: `workExecutorId` (plan), `capabilityHints`/`agentType` (`executeExecutorCli`/`executeAssignment`), và hook `resolveWork` cho `decide --work` — `dispatch/cli.mjs` không còn bộ đọc event Work riêng, không còn bản chép đồ thị stage.
  3. Work mang `workflowStep` (id bước trong Workflow của domain); `src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`, `src/state/stage-fsm.mjs` đã xoá — `domain-registry.mjs` (phần vòng đời Work của domain + tra Workflow) và `step-fsm.mjs` (cạnh chuyển bước = `transitions` của Workflow) thay thế. Chi tiết dữ liệu cũ: spec Work-State, "Work không còn `stage`".
  4. Cổng mutating của một unit-run: Assignment mutating phải mang `binding` do `bind()` sinh ra, khớp bản `bind()` tính lại từ `unit.json`, và không được ghim executor khác (`policy.preferExecutor`) — thiếu/khác → từ chối trước khi spawn.

- **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `src/state/**`, `src/workflow/**` hay bất kỳ module tầng Work (`work-compat`, `work-dispatch`, `operation-choice`, `loop`, `claim-port`, `prompt-templates`, `intake/`, `verbs/`), và không chứa literal tên domain/bước (guard `test/architecture.test.mjs`, tên đọc từ `domains/*/` trên đĩa). Cụ thể:
  1. Operation/taskSpec/skill của một bước đến từ định nghĩa Workflow (`domains/<d>/workflows/*.yaml`, `steps[].operations`/`skill`), tầng Work đọc qua `src/state/domain-registry.mjs` rồi đưa vào `buildAssignment({ domain, stage, operation, operations })`. Dispatch kiểm `operation ∈ operations` (lỗi `unknown operation ... for stage ...`), ghi danh sách hợp lệ vào `provenance.declared.legalOperations`; `executeAssignment` từ chối một Assignment declared không mang danh sách đó hoặc có `operation` ngoài danh sách (và `dispatch: human-only`). Trường `stage` trên Assignment hiện chỉ còn là nhãn mờ của bước (đổi tên theo đợt thuật ngữ).
  2. [Phần đầu vào còn lại ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only) — `work`/`workItem`/`workExecutorId` thôi là đầu vào của dispatch; `decide --work` nhận hint; `workDispatchContext` không còn trả `work`] Mọi thứ Work-aware chuyển ra tầng Work: `src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` (chọn operation cho bước hiện tại, trước ở `dispatch/`), `src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs` (`spawnWorker`, `resolveAgentTypeForWork`, `resolveWorkForDispatch`, `workDispatchContext`), `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (`executorIdForWork`, `buildPrompt`, `workCapabilityHints`). Dispatch nhận đầu vào đã phân giải: `workExecutorId` (plan), `capabilityHints`/`agentType` (`executeExecutorCli`/`executeAssignment`), và hook `resolveWork` cho `decide --work` — `dispatch/cli.mjs` không còn bộ đọc event Work riêng, không còn bản chép đồ thị stage.
  3. Work mang `workflowStep` (id bước trong Workflow của domain); `src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`, `src/state/stage-fsm.mjs` đã xoá — `domain-registry.mjs` (phần vòng đời Work của domain + tra Workflow) và `step-fsm.mjs` (cạnh chuyển bước = `transitions` của Workflow) thay thế. Chi tiết dữ liệu cũ: spec Work-State, "Work không còn `stage`".
  4. Cổng mutating của một unit-run: Assignment mutating phải mang `binding` do `bind()` sinh ra, khớp bản `bind()` tính lại từ `unit.json`, và không được ghim executor khác (`policy.preferExecutor`) — thiếu/khác → từ chối trước khi spawn.

Only `*` (inside one segment) and `**` (a whole segment, zero or more segments) are globs; every other character, `[ ] { } ! ?` included, is literal. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.

Chi tiết ở spec. +- **Supersede (một phần, không sửa tại chỗ):** phần chọn ghế của RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI), RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), RUL98 (workflow start passes --timeout and --account to each Unit), RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor), RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat), RUL106 (a seat walks a tier declared order and its cell entries) ở "Lịch sử quyết định" của file này; mỗi rule mang một dòng trỏ tới record này. Phần không phải chọn ghế giữ nguyên. +- **Điều kiện đảo:** Shape S đổi sang B nếu owner bác giao thức hai-stage không-exec-dưới-lock hoặc ngân sách exec đo được thất bại; nâng tier qua override mở lại khi có cửa chứng thực người. Chi tiết: [seat-binding.md mục 14](seat-binding.md). +- **Ranh giới:** đổi component-boundary khi code land (authority chọn ghế rời hàng Execution Core); chưa đổi hôm nay. +Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. It now comes from `ranConfinementBackend` (`settlement.mjs`): the prepared-invocation record the Confinement Authority published for the launch (`protected/prepared-invocation/.json`, backend type, `none` → `null`), else the attestation the dispatch returned with outcome `enforced`. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run. - **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

currentPassage.text: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "executor phải khai capability" đã bỏ]; partly reverses the `execute --for` retirement of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch; `execute --for` đã rút), 2026-10-13).** `execute <id>` with no purpose infers the capability from the executor's own `for` list, a required-confinement capability first (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`). RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.

A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Câu trả lời owner định hình quyết định: 20:39 (project thắng khuyến nghị tier của workflow; ghim `family#invocation` là cứng) và 21:06 (A: `prefer` là khoá duy nhất, chỉ ghế agent; B: không nâng tier bằng override đợt đầu; C: `tier` capability nằm dưới khuyến nghị workflow, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell; drain cộng doctor stop; `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor). Spec: [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md). +- **Bối cảnh:** quyết định "ghế này chạy bằng gì" bị tính ở `bind()`, `provider-capacity`, `assignment-policy`, cổng ghi và doctor, kèm hai walker; `rigor` gánh ba việc (số checker, độc lập, tier); config không có tầng ghế. +- **Quyết định:** một authority Seat Binding (crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng) trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent kèm lý do; rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập, `rigorToTier` bị xoá, tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc; cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn; năm role, workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer`; khẩu vị role, persona và ghế sống trong config capability; project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị; chỉ con người nâng tier, đợt đầu không có đường nâng bằng override; chuyển đổi một đợt có drain và điểm dừng doctor. oldPassage.text:
- **Runs when:** mọi lần `git commit` chạm cây chính — dù người gõ tay, một trợ lý,
  hay CI — đi qua một hook cài sẵn ở tầng git (không phải một verb fgOS, không phải
  một cấu hình riêng của công cụ trợ lý nào).
- **Blocked when:** đèn hoạt động (beacon, `.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json`)
  ghi rằng một danh tính KHÁC đã commit ở cây chính này trong cửa sổ `windowMs` chính
  người ghi khai (mặc định 20 s, đè được qua `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) — commit
  bị từ chối thẳng; hoặc một writer fgOS (claim, checkpoint, land) đang giữ khóa kernel
  `main-checkout` (`<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock`) mà commit này không phải con mượn
  — hook thử khóa MỘT lần bằng description riêng, không bao giờ chờ, rồi từ chối. Đèn
  hỏng thì ngược lại: chỉ là gợi ý, nên cảnh báo rồi cho qua. Commit của chính fgOS
  (git con chạy qua `runBorrowed`: `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` chỉ đúng slot, slot cùng
  `dev:ino` với file khóa, `flock` không chờ trên slot thành công) bỏ qua đèn, không ghi đèn.
- **What changes:** khi cây chính đang rảnh, hoặc khi CHÍNH danh tính đang commit là
  danh tính đã ghi khóa gần nhất (cùng phiên tiếp tục làm việc), commit đi qua bình
  thường, không thông báo gì. Danh tính ưu tiên biến môi trường phiên trợ lý khi có;
  vắng mặt (terminal tay gõ) thì suy ra từ một tiến trình tổ tiên gần đó — suy đoán
  tốt-nhất, không tuyệt đối (hai terminal tay gõ chia sẻ cùng tiến trình cha gần có
  thể không phân biệt được nhau — xem Open Gaps).
- **Side effects:** ghi đèn hoạt động (`{v:1, kind:'beacon', writer, writtenAt,
  windowMs, auditPid}`, thay nguyên tử) CUỐI hook, sau mọi kiểm tra từ chối, nên commit
  bị từ chối không để lại đèn. Hook KHÔNG lấy khóa `main-checkout`: đó là mutex kernel của
  writer fgOS, claim/land/approve/`fgctl init` không bao giờ đọc đèn, nên một commit ở
  main không chặn ai. Không đụng sổ đăng ký phiên, không đụng
  `sessions.lock`/`runner.lock`/mutex nóng `state`. `fgos return`/`cleanup`/`compound` xoá
  đèn của chính phiên (chỉ khi đúng writer); `fgos lock-status` hiện đèn ở trường
  `activity`.
- **Afterwards:** một commit bị từ chối in thông điệp giải thích bằng thời gian ("một
  phiên khác dường như đang hoạt động ở đây gần đây") và trỏ người tới đúng cách mở
  một cây làm việc cô lập — không bao giờ in ra một định danh thô (pid/session-id) như
  thể đó là thứ người đọc cần tự hành động theo.
